name: MC78L12ABDR2G
title: 100 mA fixed positive voltage regulators, MC78L00A series and NCV78L00A
summary: A family of three-terminal linear regulators giving a fixed positive output of 5, 8, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 24 V at up to 100 mA. Current limiting and thermal shutdown are built in, and many uses need no external parts. Parts come in TO−92, SOIC−8 and SOT−89, in a 0 to 125 °C (AC) and a −40 to 125 °C (AB) grade, with NCV automotive versions. The MC78L12ABDR2G is the 12 V, −40 °C grade in SOIC−8 on tape and reel.

notes: A part number ending * is an NCV part: AEC−Q100 qualified, PPAP capable, for automotive and other uses needing site and change control. For NCV78L05A, NCV78L12A and NCV78L15A, Tlow = −40°C and Thigh = +125°C are guaranteed by design.
All packages are Pb−free.

circuits.title: Standard application
circuits.description: The basic hookup for any output voltage: a 0.33 µF capacitor across the input and 0.1 µF across the output, with input and output sharing one ground. The input cap is needed when the regulator sits far from the supply's filter capacitor; stability does not depend on the output cap, which sharpens transient response.
notes: Input should stay about 2.0 V above output, including at the bottom of the input ripple.

circuits.title: Current regulator
circuits.description: A 5 V part set up as a current source into a grounded load. R sits between OUT and the GND pin, and the load current leaves from the GND pin, so it equals the 5 V across R plus the regulator's own bias current. The 5 V part is picked to keep dissipation down. For 100 mA, R is 50 Ω rated 1/2 W, and the load may swing up to about 7 V below the input.

parts.note: sets the current; 50 Ω, 1/2 W for 100 mA

circuits.title: ±15 V tracking voltage regulator
circuits.description: An MC78L15A makes +VO from +20 V. Two 10 k resistors run from +VO to −VO; their midpoint goes to the inverting input of an MC1741 op amp whose non-inverting input is grounded. The op amp runs from +VO (pin 7) and the 20V input (pin 4), and its output drives the base of an MPS U55 PNP whose collector is on the 20V input and whose emitter reaches −VO through 6.5 Ω. An MPS A70 PNP has its collector on the U55 base and its base and emitter on −VO. Each input has 0.33 µF to ground.
notes: U2 pin numbers: 2 IN−, 3 IN+, 4 V−, 6 OUT, 7 V+.

circuits.title: Positive and negative regulator
circuits.description: A positive MC78LXXA and a negative MC79LXXA share one ground to give a split supply. Each input has 0.33 µF to ground and each output 0.1 µF to ground.

operation.text: An internal current limit caps the output current under a short, and a thermal overload circuit turns the regulator off when it gets too hot. Package dissipation is internally limited.

Input and output need a common ground. Keep the input about 2.0 V above the output, also at the low point of any ripple. Dropout is 1.7 V typical at 25 °C and 40 mA, and falls as junction temperature rises.

Many low-current uses need no capacitors at all. Bypass the input when long wires lead from the supply filter or when the load has a lot of capacitance: 0.33 µF or more, tantalum, mylar or another type with low impedance at high frequency, mounted with short leads right at the input and ground pins. An output bypass is also advised; stability does not depend on it, but transient response is better with it.
There is no remote sense pin, so lay out to avoid ground loops and voltage drops in the leads.

The SOIC−8 is a modified SO−8: pins 2, 3, 6 and 7 are tied to the die flag, which lowers its thermal resistance and lets it dissipate more when those pins are soldered to copper. Its outside dimensions match a standard SO−8. RθJA falls from about 158 °C/W at zero copper length to about 38 °C/W at 50 mm pads, and allowed dissipation at 50 °C ambient rises from about 0.6 W to 2.6 W.

AC parts are specified for TJ from 0 to +125 °C, AB parts for −40 to +125 °C. Parts with the NCV prefix (NCV78L05A, 08A, 12A, 15A and 24A in the ordering list) are for automotive and other uses needing site and change control, AEC−Q100 qualified and PPAP capable; for NCV78L05A, NCV78L12A and NCV78L15A the −40 to +125 °C limits are guaranteed by design. 18 V and 24 V come only in TO−92; the SOT−89 holds the 5 V AC part only.

Fixed outputs of 5, 8, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 24 V at up to 100 mA. The MC79L00A series is the matching negative regulator. Against a zener and resistor, the regulator has much lower output impedance and quiescent current.
